speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; to begin our evaluation, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any redness or warmth in the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Gamekeeper's Thumb (Stener lesion) / Ulnar collateral ligament injury of the MCP joint.

*Correction based on your specific symptom of "ring finger" pain:* Given the mechanism of injury (jerking of an outstretched finger) and the location of pain/swelling in the right ring finger, I suspect an injury to the ulnar collateral ligament of the ring finger or a tendon injury. To confirm the extent of the ligament damage and rule out fracture, REQUEST TEST: X-Ray of right hand. REQUEST IMAGES: Ultrasound of right ring finger MCP joint.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
